subject: New subprocessor addition & DPIA items for Atlas Payments
messages:
From: Elena Moro <elena.moro@atlas-payments.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.com
Cc: security@atlas-payments.com
Date: 2026-01-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: New subprocessor addition & DPIA items for Atlas Payments

Hi Ava,

Quick heads-up: Atlas is planning to add a payment service provider (VectorCloud Payments) as a subprocessor for card tokenization and settlement. This will involve an onward transfer of transaction metadata and tokenized identifiers. Before we proceed with onboarding, our compliance team needs a few items from Redwood so we can complete our DPIA and update our vendor inventory: 

- Confirmation that Redwood allows onward transfers to audited PSPs and any standard contractual safeguards you require (SCCs / DPA clauses).
- A current subprocessor roster (CSV) showing active subprocessors and effective dates.
- Most recent SOC 2 summary / AT report (redacted acceptable).
- Copy of your Data Processing Addendum (DPA) or a pointer to the clause we should reference.
- Any special limits on cross-border transfers (if applicable) and whether you process EU data in a manner that would require SCCs.

We'd like to close this item by EOD 2026-01-17 if possible — VectorCloud is aiming to go live in late January.

I attached our onboarding checklist for context. Let me know if you want to route technical questions to our security contact (cc'd).

Thanks,
Elena Moro
Head of Vendor Risk — Atlas Payments
elena.moro@atlas-payments.com

Attachment: onboarding_packet_atlas_20260110.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: 2026-01-11T11:20:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: New subprocessor addition & DPIA items for Atlas Payments

Folks — forwarding Atlas' request (below). They've flagged VectorCloud as a prospective subprocessor and need the usual artifacts + confirmation on onward transfers / SCCs. Can you advise on the following by EOD Tue?

Questions / proposed approach:
- Do we consent to onboarding VectorCloud for tokenization/settlement? (high-level: allowed for audited PSPs, but require DPA + SCCs where applicable)
- What specific artifacts can we share from the roster and SOC2 without legal review?
- Any red flags for VectorCloud (we don't have them on the roster today).

Suggested quick reply: we can provide a trimmed roster + SOC2 summary and share our standard DPA; we require that processors sign our DPA (or we sign SCCs if EU data involved) and that subprocessor binds to equivalent security controls. Legal to confirm.

I attached our subprocessor policy and a lightweight reply template I was going to use. Monica — can you take point on legal text? Vivek — can you flag any technical limits (e.g., no persistent PAN storage, token-only flows)?

Thanks,
Ava
Product Partnerships — Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0104

Date: 2026-01-13T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: New subprocessor addition & DPIA items for Atlas Payments

Ava — I reviewed Atlas' asks. TL;DR: we can approve conditional onboarding for audited PSPs like VectorCloud, provided legal sign-off on DPA/SCCs and we only share limited artifacts. Below is a draft reply and a shortlist of items we should attach.

High level position (for reply):
- Redwood permits onward transfers to subprocessors that meet our security and audit requirements (SOC2 Type II or equivalent) and agree to contractual obligations consistent with our DPA.
- For EU-origin data we expect SCCs or an equivalent transfer mechanism if VectorCloud will act as a controller/processor in a third country.
- We require that subprocessors adhere to our non-persistent PAN/token storage rules — tokenization-only flows OK.

Items cleared to share today (internal approval):
- Redacted subprocessor roster (CSV) — include names, service purpose, effective dates (no internal contact emails).
- SOC2 summary (one-page redacted cover/controls summary).
- Copy of our standard DPA and the specific processor appendix.

Items requiring legal review / redaction: full SOC2 report (external counsel), detailed network diagrams, encryption key rotation schedules.

Draft reply (paste into email to Atlas):
"Hi Elena — thanks for the heads-up. We can support onboarding of VectorCloud subject to the requirements below. Attached: a redacted subprocessor roster, a SOC2 controls summary, and our standard DPA for review. Please confirm whether VectorCloud will process EU personal data and whether Atlas will require SCCs; if so we will engage legal to execute SCCs as appropriate. Also please share any DPIA findings Atlas needs to capture about VectorCloud once you have them.

We also note that Redwood operators do not perform persistent PAN storage and require token-only flows for payment processors; please confirm VectorCloud's handling of tokens vs raw PAN.

If you want, Monica can coordinate DPA/SCC signatures and Evelyn can intake any technical questionnaires from VectorCloud for our security team.

Best,
Vivek
"

Action items: Monica to run legal check on our DPA -> target 48h; Evelyn to flag any security exceptions if VectorCloud requests special crypto or key access. Ava to send Atlas the cleared artifacts and draft reply.

Attachments to include in outgoing to Atlas: redwood_subprocessor_roster_20260113.csv, redwood_soca_summary_2025.pdf, redwood_dpa_signed_v3.pdf

--
Vivek Kulkarni
VP Infrastructure & Security — Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0123
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Elena Moro <elena.moro@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: security@atlas-payments.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: 2026-01-14T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: New subprocessor addition & DPIA items for Atlas Payments

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads-up and the onboarding packet. We've reviewed internally and can proceed with conditional consent for VectorCloud to act as a subprocessor for tokenization/settlement, subject to the items below.

What we're sharing now (attached):
- redwood_subprocessor_roster_20260113.csv (redacted roster: names, service purpose, effective dates)
- redwood_soca_summary_2025.pdf (one-page SOC2 controls summary)
- redwood_dpa_signed_v3.pdf (our standard DPA / processor appendix)

Conditions / next steps:
1) Please confirm whether VectorCloud will process EU personal data. If yes, Atlas should confirm whether SCCs are required; we will engage legal to execute SCCs or equivalent transfer mechanisms as needed.
2) VectorCloud must agree to adhere to our processor obligations (DPA) and to token-only flows — Redwood does not permit persistent PAN storage by downstream subprocessors.
3) If Atlas or VectorCloud would like the unredacted SOC2 report or more detailed diagrams, please raise a formal request; legal will assess and manage redaction.

We can also provide a short answers packet for your DPIA (controls mapping to common DPIA questions) once you confirm VectorCloud's processing scope. Monica will coordinate DPA/SCC signature logistics; Evelyn is copied for any technical/security questionnaires.

Let me know if you need anything else to close your DPIA.

Best regards,
Ava Chen
Product Partnerships — Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0104

Attachments: redwood_subprocessor_roster_20260113.csv (CSV), redwood_soca_summary_2025.pdf (PDF), redwood_dpa_signed_v3.pdf (PDF)
